summary: This Docker stage sets up a production build of Docusaurus, a documentation site generator. It installs Docusaurus from scratch, copies in the project's dependencies and source code, then builds the final static website files.

explanations.1: This starts a new Docker build stage called 'building_production' that builds on top of a 'base' image defined elsewhere.
explanations.4: This runs the Docusaurus setup wizard non-interactively to create a new Docusaurus project in the /opt/docusaurus folder with the classic template and JavaScript (not TypeScript).
explanations.7: After installing Docusaurus, this changes the owner of all files in the directory to the 'node' user so that the non-root node user can work with those files later.
explanations.13: This copies the package.json and yarn.lock files from your local machine into the Docker container before installing dependencies, so Docker can cache the dependency installation if these files haven't changed.
explanations.16: The --immutable flag tells yarn to fail if it would change the lock file, ensuring everyone gets exactly the same dependency versions.
explanations.19: This copies all your actual documentation source code (markdown files, custom components, config, etc.) into the container.
explanations.22: This runs the build command, which compiles all the markdown and React components into static HTML/CSS/JavaScript files ready to be served.
